data.scope: United States, privately held nongovernmental manufacturer using US GAAP and FIFO/weighted-average inventory; March 31, 2026 close, with a separate June 30, 2026 custom-contract branch. examples.label: Synthetic process/batch mass and cost close
examples.policy: Weighted-average single batch, no opening WIP. All conversion assumed uniform through the batch. Normal loss is absorbed by output; recoverable scrap is credited at assumed $10/kg net recoverable value. The scrap policy is a declared illustrative assumption pending current US policy review.
examples.normal_capacity_evidence: Synthetic approved CAP-0331 assumes actual activity is abnormally below the documented normal-capacity range, after planned maintenance. A ratio alone does not establish abnormal activity.

abnormal_loss_branch.assumption: Reclassify the 50 kg loss as abnormal, with uniform incurred resources. Illustrative cost attribution assigns 5% of materials and applied conversion to the loss; no assertion that FAS 151 prescribes this attribution.

byproduct_branch.trigger: Two saleable primary outputs or material by-product value
byproduct_branch.disposition: Do not apply the immaterial-scrap residual convention automatically. Retain separate quantities, split-off point, further processing costs and sales values; approve a joint-cost policy using current ASC guidance. No numerical joint-cost conclusion is asserted.

examples.label: Synthetic discrete manufacturing equivalent-unit WIP
examples.policy: Separate job, no beginning WIP. All materials introduced at start; completed units 100% converted; remaining WIP 40% converted. Weighted-average equivalent units are an illustrative cost-system assumption.
examples.rounding: Round completed conversion to cents; WIP conversion is the remaining cents, a disclosed rounding allocation of less than one cent before rounding. No inventory plug.

examples.label: Synthetic outsourced ownership and late-invoice close
contract_assumptions: Signed TOLL-01 retains manufacturer ownership and control of identifiable components and output; processor cannot redirect or pledge them.
Processor confirmation CONF-0331 reports 900 completed and 100 unfinished components; unfinished units have received no conversion service.
Conversion service completed March 31 is $1350; invoice INV-0403 arrives April 3; no separate additional fee or opening payable.

counterexamples.decision: Exclude customer-owned material from the processor inventory population under the stated no-control facts; assess service revenue separately.
Custody and a warehouse count cannot establish acquisition. Read control, return, payment and redirection terms before recognition.
Track custody separately; no tooling asset conclusion from physical location. Reuse asset foundations and inspect control and contract terms.
Ownership conclusion unresolved. Keep confirmed quantities in an exception register and withhold automatic inventory recognition.

examples.label: Synthetic custom-contract timing and scope counterexample
qualifying_facts: No alternative use is supported at contract inception by substantive contractual and practical restrictions.
Enforceable right to payment for performance to date includes a reasonable profit margin on cancellation other than manufacturer breach; legal review is assumed solely for this synthetic branch.
Single performance obligation; all incurred costs depict performance, no excluded inefficiency, uninstalled material, variable consideration, financing or collectibility complication.

facts: Standard equipment can be redirected to another customer.
No enforceable right to payment for performance to date.
Customer does not control WIP and does not simultaneously receive and consume the production benefits.
counterexample.decision: None of ASC 606-10-25-27 criteria is established. Recognize at point-in-time control transfer when supported; do not use 50% completion to book revenue. If payment rights are merely unknown, conclusion remains unresolved rather than automatically point-in-time.

examples.remaining_gap: Contract loss, modifications, tooling ownership and asset/labor capitalization questions route to #119/#120/#123; their completion is not asserted.

examples.label: Synthetic FIFO write-down branch on PROC-0331 good output
examples.boundary: Separate sensitivity applied to the normal-loss branch only; do not add it to the abnormal-loss branch. LIFO/retail is outside this calculation. FAS 151 footnote 2 describes reduced year-end cost as subsequent cost; interim recovery and current US exceptions require separate review. Do not import the IFRS reversal rule.

examples.label: Synthetic quantity-to-ledger cutoff register

events.evidence: Material issue 1000 kg, count signed March 31
events.treatment: Reconcile input to 900 good, 50 scrap, 50 loss; cost and physical ledgers separately.

events.evidence: 80 complete, 20 WIP at 40% conversion; independent routing-stage signoff
events.treatment: Include finished goods and WIP at their separate conversion stages.

events.evidence: Shipment of all 80 finished units; contract transfers control at shipment; no bill-and-hold or over-time terms
events.treatment: March: retain 1472727 cents finished goods and zero related revenue/COGS. April: Dr COGS 1472727, Cr finished goods 1472727. Sales price is not supplied; no invented revenue amount.
Accrue 135000 cents fee in March and include confirmed manufacturer-owned units.

events.evidence: Invoice references March service and accrual key
events.treatment: Clear March accrual to AP; do not capitalize fee again.

examples.control: Match event IDs to lot, count, production completion, shipment contract, accrual and GL. Reconcile opening plus receipts/issues/conversion less disposals to close. Reconcile missing documents and duplicate invoice keys, not just balanced debit/credit totals.
examples.counterexample: Removing CONF-TOLL does not prove zero stock or zero accrual. Mark ownership/quantity/service evidence incomplete and request corroboration; never force a balancing plug.
